record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: If X is a consonant T0 space, is its Hoare power space PH(X), the lower Vietoris space of nonempty closed subsets of X, also consonant?

evidence.quote: Question 6.16. ([5]) For a consonant T0 space X, is PH (X) also consonant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let X be a topological space. The space X is called T0 if for any two distinct points there is an open set containing exactly one of them. Recall the following definitions.

(1) The upper Kuratowski topology on the set K(X) of compact saturated subsets (where a set is saturated if it equals the intersection of its open neighborhoods) is generated as follows: a family A ⊆ K(X) is open iff it is Scott-open in the poset (K(X), ⊇) — that is, A is an upper set under ⊇ and, whenever a filtered intersection of compact saturated sets belongs to A, some element of the filtered family already does. Equivalently, one works with the lattice O(X) of open sets of X equipped with the co-compact topology.

(2) The co-compact (or upper Vietoris-type) topology on O(X) is the topology whose basic open sets are {U ∈ O(X) : K ⊆ U} for K ranging over compact saturated subsets of X.

A T0 space X is called consonant if the co-compact topology on O(X) equals the Scott topology on (O(X), ⊆); equivalently, every Scott-open family of open sets of X is a union of sets of the form {U ∈ O(X) : K ⊆ U} for K compact saturated.

(3) The Hoare power space (lower powerspace) PH(X) of X is defined as follows. Its underlying set is the collection of nonempty closed subsets of X. Its topology is the lower Vietoris topology, which is generated by the subbasic open sets ◊U = {F ∈ PH(X) : F ∩ U ≠ ∅} for U ranging over open subsets of X.

Question. Suppose X is a consonant T0 space. Is the Hoare power space PH(X) also consonant?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., the 2025 Acta Mathematica Sinica paper by He and Zhao "Some Problems about Consonant and Co-Consonant Spaces", and its 2022 arXiv preprint) addresses consonance/co-consonance of powerspace constructions but only obtains results for the co-consonance side: it is shown that co-consonance of PH(X) implies co-consonance of X, and that PH(ΣP) is co-consonant for continuous posets P. The question of whether consonance of a T0 space X transfers to consonance of the Hoare power space PH(X) (attributed to de Brecht and Kawai) appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some Problems about Consonant and Co-Consonant Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: if the lower powerspace PH(X) is co-consonant, then X is co-consonant; ... for a continuous poset P, PH(ΣP) is co-consonant.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results address co-consonance of PH(X), not the consonance question; the consonance version is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Some problems about co-consonance of topological spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Preprint version studying co-consonance for Smyth and lower powerspaces.
status_evidence.claim: The arXiv version treats co-consonance variants and does not resolve the consonance question for PH(X).

status_evidence.title: Some new, easy facts on consonant spaces (Non-Hausdorff Topology and Domain Theory)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of consonance for hyperspaces, including open questions by de Brecht and Kawai.
status_evidence.claim: The transfer of consonance to the Hoare hyperspace is mentioned as an open problem.
